mn85:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling amongst the Bhaggas in the Deer Park in Bhesakaḷā’s Wood on the Crocodile Hill.
mn85:2.1: Then at that time Prince Bodhi’s palace named Pink Lotus was not long made, and had not been lived in by any ascetic or brāhmaṇa or human being.
mn85:3.1: Then Prince Bodhi addressed the student Sañjikāputta,
mn85:3.2: saying: “Go, dear Sañjikāputta, and approach the Fortunate One, and after approaching, worship the Fortunate One’s feet with your head in my name, and ask whether he is free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably, (and say):
mn85:3.3: ‘Prince Bodhi, reverend Sir, worships with his head at the Fortunate One’s feet, and asks whether you are free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably.’
mn85:3.5: ‘May the Fortunate One consent, reverend Sir, to Prince Bodhi (offering him) a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks.’”
mn85:4.1: “Very well, dear Sir,” said the student Sañjikāputta, and after replying to Prince Bodhi, he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One,
mn85:4.2: and after exchanging courteous talk and greetings, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side the student Sañjikāputta said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:4.3: “Prince Bodhi, dear Gotama, worships with his head at dear Gotama’s feet, and asks whether you are free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably.
mn85:4.5: ‘May the venerable Gotama consent to Prince Bodhi (offering him) a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks.’”
mn85:4.6: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.
mn85:4.7: Then the student Sañjikāputta, having understood the Fortunate One’s consent, after rising from his seat approached Prince Bodhi, and after approaching, he said this to Prince Bodhi:
mn85:4.8: “We spoke your words to dear Gotama,
mn85:4.9: saying: ‘Prince Bodhi, dear Gotama, worships with his head at dear Gotama’s feet, and asks whether you are free from sickness, free from illness, in good health, and living comfortably.
mn85:4.11: “May the venerable Gotama consent to Prince Bodhi (offering him) a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks”.’
mn85:5.1: Then Prince Bodhi, after the night had passed, having had excellent foodstuffs made ready in his own residence, and after covering the Pink Lotus palace with white cloth up to the last step, addressed the student Sañjikāputta:
mn85:5.2: saying: “Go, dear Sañjikāputta, and approach the Fortunate One, and after approaching announce the time to the Fortunate One,
mn85:5.3: saying: ‘It is time, dear Gotama, the meal is ready.’”
mn85:5.4: “Very well, dear Sir,” said the student Sañjikāputta, and after replying to Prince Bodhi, he approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he announced the time to the Fortunate One,
mn85:5.5: saying: “It is time, dear Gotama, the meal is ready.”
mn85:6.1: Then the Fortunate One, after dressing in the morning time, and picking up his bowl and robe, approached Prince Bodhi’s residence.
mn85:7.1: Then at that time Prince Bodhi was standing outside the doorway waiting for the Fortunate One.
mn85:7.2: Prince Bodhi saw the Fortunate One approaching from afar,
mn85:7.3: and after seeing him, and coming out, worshipping, and putting the Fortunate One in front, he approached the Pink Lotus palace.
mn85:7.4: Then the Fortunate One stood near the last step on the staircase.
mn85:7.5: Then Prince Bodhi said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:7.6: “May the Fortunate One ascend the cloth, reverend Sir, may the Happy One ascend the cloth,
mn85:7.7: that for a long time will be for my benefit and happiness.”
mn85:7.8: When this was said, the Fortunate One remained silent.
mn85:7.9: Then for a second time Prince Bodhi said this to the Fortunate One: “May the Fortunate One ascend the cloth, reverend Sir, may the Happy One ascend the cloth, that for a long time will be for my benefit and happiness.” Then for a second time the Fortunate One remained silent.
mn85:7.10: Then for a third time Prince Bodhi said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:7.11: “May the Fortunate One ascend the cloth, reverend Sir, may the Happy One ascend the cloth,
mn85:7.12: that for a long time will be for my benefit and happiness.”
mn85:7.13: Then the Fortunate One looked at venerable Ānanda.
mn85:7.14: Then venerable Ānanda said this to Prince Bodhi:
mn85:7.16: the Fortunate One does not walk on cloth coverings.
mn85:7.17: The Realised One looks to people in the future.”
mn85:8.1: Then Prince Bodhi, after folding up the cloth, prepared the seats on the Pink Lotus palace.
mn85:8.2: Then the Fortunate One, having ascended the Pink Lotus palace, sat down on the prepared seat, together with the Community of monks.
mn85:9.1: Then Prince Bodhi served and satisfied with his own hand the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent food and drinks.
mn85:9.2: Then Prince Bodhi, when the Fortunate One had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, after taking a low seat, sat down on one side.
mn85:9.3: While seated on one side Prince Bodhi said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:9.5: ‘Happiness is not gained through pleasure, happiness is only gained through pain.’”
mn85:10.1: “To me also, Prince, before the Awakening, while still an unawakened Bodhisatta this (thought) occurred:
mn85:10.2: ‘Happiness is not gained through pleasure, happiness is only gained through pain.’”
mn85:11.1: Then at another time, Prince, while still a youth, having beautiful black hair, endowed with auspicious youthfulness, in the prime of life, though my Mother and Father didn’t like it, and were crying with tearful faces, after shaving off my hair and beard, and donning brown garments, I went forth from the home to the homeless life.
mn85:11.2: When I had gone forth thus, searching for what was wholesome, the unsurpassed, noble and peaceful state, I approached Āḷāra Kālāma, and after approaching, I said this to Āḷāra Kālāma:
mn85:11.3: “I desire, friend Kālāma, to lead the spiritual life in this Dhamma and Discipline.”
mn85:11.4: When this was said, Prince, Āḷāra Kālāma said this to me:
mn85:11.6: venerable, this Dhamma is such that a wise man in no long time, having deep knowledge himself of what comes from his own teacher, can live, having directly experienced and attained it.”
mn85:11.7: Then, Prince, in no long time I had soon mastered that Dhamma.
mn85:11.8: Then, Prince, after a little time, merely through beating my lips, merely through repeating the prattling, I spoke knowingly about that teaching and confidently about that teaching, claiming: ‘I know, I see.’ Both I and others also.
mn85:11.9: Then this occurred to me, monks:
mn85:11.10: ‘Āḷāra Kālāma did not declare: “Through mere faith in this Dhamma alone, I have deep knowledge of it myself, I live, having directly experienced and attained it,”
mn85:11.11: for sure Āḷāra Kālāma lives knowing and seeing this Dhamma.’
mn85:12.1: Then, Prince, I approached Āḷāra Kālāma, and after approaching, I said this to Āḷāra Kālāma:
mn85:12.2: “In what way, friend Kālāma, do you declare: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it?”
mn85:12.3: When this was said, Prince, Āḷāra Kālāma declared the Sphere of Nothingness.
mn85:12.4: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:12.5: ‘There is not faith for Āḷāra Kālāma (alone), for me also there is faith,
mn85:12.6: there is not energy for Āḷāra Kālāma (alone), for me also there is energy,
mn85:12.7: there is not mindfulness for Āḷāra Kālāma (alone), for me also there is mindfulness,
mn85:12.8: there is not concentration for Āḷāra Kālāma (alone), for me also there is concentration,
mn85:12.9: there is not wisdom for Āḷāra Kālāma (alone), for me also there is wisdom.
mn85:12.10: What if, in regard to the Dhamma that Āḷāra Kālāma declares: “I have deep knowledge of it myself, I live, having directly experienced and attained it,” I were to strive to realise that Dhamma?’
mn85:12.11: Then, Prince, in no long time, soon having deep knowledge of that Dhamma myself, I lived, having directly experienced and attained it.
mn85:12.12: Then, Prince, I approached Āḷāra Kālāma, and after approaching, I said this to Āḷāra Kālāma:
mn85:12.13: “Is it in this way, friend Kālāma, that you declare: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it?”
mn85:12.14: “In this way, friend, I do declare: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it.”
mn85:12.15: “In this way I also, friend, say: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, I live, having directly experienced and attained it.”
mn85:12.16: “It is a gain for us, friend, it is a great gain for us, friend,
mn85:12.17: that we see such a venerable with us in the spiritual life.
mn85:12.18: Thus I declare I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it, and you have deep knowledge of this Dhamma yourself, and live, having directly experienced and attained it. You have deep knowledge of this Dhamma yourself, and live, having directly experienced and attained it,
mn85:12.19: and I declare I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it.
mn85:12.20: Thus the Dhamma I know is the Dhamma you know, the Dhamma you know is the Dhamma I know.
mn85:12.21: Thus as I am, so are you, as you are, so am I.
mn85:12.22: Come now, friend, the two of us will look after this group.”
mn85:12.23: “Thus my teacher Āḷāra Kālāma, Prince, placed me, the pupil, as equal, and in the very same position as himself, and worshipped me with the highest worship.
mn85:12.24: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:12.25: ‘This Dhamma does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation to peace, to deep knowledge, to Complete Awakening, to Nibbāna, but only as far as rebirth in the Sphere of Nothingness.’
mn85:12.26: Then, Prince, having not found satisfaction in that Dhamma, I was therefore disgusted with that Dhamma and went away.
mn85:12.27: Then, Prince, still searching for what was wholesome, the unsurpassed, noble and peaceful state, I approached Uddaka Rāmaputta, and after approaching, I said this to Uddaka Rāmaputta:
mn85:12.28: “I desire, friend, to lead the spiritual life in this Dhamma and Discipline.”
mn85:12.29: When this was said, Prince, Uddaka Rāmaputta said this to me:
mn85:12.31: venerable, this Dhamma is such that a wise man in no long time, having deep knowledge himself of what comes from his own teacher, can live, having directly experienced and attained it.”
mn85:12.32: Then in no long time, Prince, soon I had mastered that Dhamma.
mn85:12.33: Then, Prince, after a little time I indeed, merely through beating my lips, merely through repeating the prattling, spoke knowingly about that teaching and confidently about that teaching, claiming: ‘I know, I see.’ Both I and others also.
mn85:12.34: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:12.35: ‘Rāma did not declare: “Through mere faith in this Dhamma alone, having knowledge of it myself, I live, having directly experienced and attained it,”
mn85:12.36: for sure Rāma lived knowing and seeing this Dhamma.’
mn85:13.1: Then, Prince, I approached Uddaka Rāmaputta, and after approaching, I said this to Uddaka Rāmaputta:
mn85:13.2: “In what way, friend, did Rāma declare: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it?”
mn85:13.3: When this was said, Prince, Uddaka Rāmaputta declared the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception.
mn85:13.4: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:13.5: ‘There was not faith for Rāma (alone), for me also there is faith,
mn85:13.6: there was not energy for Rāma (alone), for me also there is energy,
mn85:13.7: there was not mindfulness for Rāma (alone), for me also there is mindfulness,
mn85:13.8: there was not concentration for Rāma (alone), for me also there is concentration,
mn85:13.9: there was not wisdom for Rāma (alone), for me also there is wisdom.
mn85:13.10: What if, in regard to the Dhamma that Rāma declared: I have deep knowledge of it myself, I live, having directly experienced and attained it, I were to strive to realise that Dhamma?’
mn85:13.11: Then, Prince, in no long time, soon having deep knowledge of that Dhamma myself, I lived, having directly experienced and attained it.
mn85:13.12: Then, Prince, I approached Uddaka Rāmaputta, and after approaching, I said this to Uddaka Rāmaputta:
mn85:13.13: “Is it in this way, friend, that Rāma declared: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, having directly experienced and attained it?”
mn85:13.14: “In this way, friend, Rāma did declare he had deep knowledge of this Dhamma himself, having directly experienced and attained it.”
mn85:13.15: “In this way, friend, I also say: I have deep knowledge of this Dhamma myself, I live, having directly experienced and attained it.”
mn85:13.16: “It is a gain for us, friend, it is a great gain for us, friend,
mn85:13.17: that we see such a venerable with us in the spiritual life.
mn85:13.18: Thus Rāma declared he had deep knowledge of this Dhamma himself, having directly experienced and attained it, and you have deep knowledge of this Dhamma yourself, you live, having directly experienced and attained it.
mn85:13.19: And that Dhamma you have deep knowledge of yourself, you live, having directly experienced and attained it, that Rāma declared he had deep knowledge of that Dhamma himself, having directly experienced and attained it.
mn85:13.20: Thus the Dhamma Rāma knew is the Dhamma you know, the Dhamma you know is the Dhamma Rāma knew.
mn85:13.21: Thus as Rāma was, so are you, as you are, so was Rāma.
mn85:13.22: Come now, friend, you will look after this group.”
mn85:13.23: Thus my friend in the spiritual life, Uddaka Rāmaputta, Prince, placed me in the teacher’s position, and worshipped me with the highest worship.
mn85:13.24: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:13.25: ‘This Dhamma does not lead to disenchantment, or to dispassion, or to cessation, or to peace, or to deep knowledge, or to Complete Awakening, or to Nibbāna, but only as far as rebirth in the Sphere of Neither-Perception-nor-Non-Perception.’
mn85:13.26: Then, Prince, having not found satisfaction in that Dhamma, I was therefore disgusted with that Dhamma and went away.
mn85:14.1: Then, Prince, still searching for what was wholesome, the unsurpassed, noble and peaceful state, while walking gradually on walking tour I entered Magadha, and arrived at the Army town at Uruvelā.
mn85:14.2: There I saw a delightful piece of land, and a pleasing jungle thicket, with a clear river flowing and lovely banks, and nearby a village suitable for collecting alms.
mn85:14.3: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:14.4: ‘Delightful is this piece of land, with its pleasing jungle thicket, and a clear river flowing and lovely banks, and it is near a village suitable for collecting alms.
mn85:14.5: I thought: ‘This is surely enough for the striving of a son of a good family who is seeking to strive.’
mn85:14.6: Then, Prince, I sat down right there,
mn85:15.1: Then, Prince, these three wonderful similes occurred to me, that were unheard of in the past.
mn85:16.1: Suppose, Prince, there were a green, sappy timber, lying in water,
mn85:16.2: and a man would come with an upper kindling wood,
mn85:16.3: thinking: ‘I will make fire, I will engender heat.’
mn85:16.4: What do you think, Prince, would that man
mn85:16.5: with that green, sappy timber, lying in water, through rubbing with the upper kindling wood be able to make fire, to engender heat?”
mn85:16.7: What is the reason for that? Because, dear Gotama,
mn85:16.8: it is a green, sappy timber, and it is lying in water.
mn85:16.9: That man would only get a fair share of weariness and vexation.”
mn85:17.1: Just so, Prince, whatever ascetics and priests live unsecluded from sensual pleasures with their body and mind, who, in regard to sensual desire for sensual pleasures, love for sensual pleasures, infatuation for sensual pleasures, thirst for sensual pleasures and fever for sensual pleasures, without having completely abandoned them on the inside, without having completely allayed them,
mn85:17.2: even if those good ascetics and priests feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, they are incapable of knowledge and insight into the supreme and complete Awakening,
mn85:17.3: and even if those good ascetics and priests do not feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, still they are incapable of knowledge and insight into the supreme and complete Awakening.
mn85:17.4: This, Prince, is the first wonderful simile that occurred to me, that was unheard of in the past.
mn85:18.1: Then, Prince, a second wonderful simile occurred to me, that was unheard of in the past.
mn85:18.2: Suppose, Prince, there were a green, sappy timber, far from the water, lying on the ground,
mn85:18.3: and a man would come with an upper kindling wood,
mn85:18.4: thinking: ‘I will make fire, I will engender heat.’
mn85:18.5: What do you think, Prince, would that man
mn85:18.6: with that green, sappy timber, far from the water, lying on the ground, through rubbing with the upper kindling wood be able to make fire, to engender heat?”
mn85:18.8: What is the reason for that? Because, dear Gotama,
mn85:18.9: it is (still) a green, sappy timber, however far it is from the water, lying on the ground.
mn85:18.10: That man would only get a fair share of weariness and vexation.”
mn85:18.11: “Just so, Prince, whatever ascetics and priests live secluded from sensual pleasures with their body and mind, who, in regard to sensual desire for sensual pleasures, love for sensual pleasures, infatuation for sensual pleasures, thirst for sensual pleasures and fever for sensual pleasures, without having completely abandoned them on the inside, without having completely allayed them,
mn85:18.12: even if those good ascetics and priests feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, they are incapable of knowledge and insight into the supreme and complete Awakening;
mn85:18.13: and even if those good ascetics and priests do not feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, (still) they are incapable of knowledge and insight into the supreme and complete Awakening.
mn85:18.14: This, Prince, is the second wonderful simile that occurred to me, that was unheard of in the past.
mn85:19.1: Then, Prince, a third wonderful simile occurred to me, that was unheard of in the past.
mn85:19.2: Suppose, Prince, there were a dry, sapless timber, far from the water, lying on the ground,
mn85:19.3: and a man would come with an upper kindling wood,
mn85:19.4: thinking: ‘I will make fire, I will engender heat.’
mn85:19.5: What do you think, Prince, would that man
mn85:19.6: with that dry, sapless timber, far from the water, lying on the ground, through rubbing with the upper kindling wood be able to make fire, to engender heat?”
mn85:19.8: What is the reason for that? Because, dear Gotama,
mn85:19.9: it is a dry, sapless timber, and it is far from the water, lying on the ground.”
mn85:19.10: “Just so, Prince, whatever ascetics and priests live secluded from sensual pleasures with their body and mind, who, in regard to sensual desire for sensual pleasures, love for sensual pleasures, infatuation for sensual pleasures, thirst for sensual pleasures and fever for sensual pleasures, have completely abandoned them on the inside, completely allayed them,
mn85:19.11: even if those good ascetics and priests feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, they are capable of knowledge and insight into the supreme and complete Awakening;
mn85:19.12: and even if those good ascetics and priests do not feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, (still) they are capable of knowledge and insight into the supreme and complete Awakening.
mn85:19.13: This, Prince, is the third wonderful simile that occurred to me, that was unheard of in the past.
mn85:19.14: These, Prince, are the three wonderful similes that occurred to me, that were unheard of in the past.
mn85:20.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:20.2: ‘What if I, with teeth clenched against teeth, with the tongue pressing on the palate, were to completely restrain, constrain and suppress one thought with (another) thought.’
mn85:20.3: Then I, Prince, with teeth clenched against teeth, with the tongue pressing on the palate, did completely restrain, constrain and suppress one thought with (another) thought.
mn85:20.4: Then to me, Prince, with teeth clenched against teeth, with the tongue pressing on the palate, with complete restraint, constraint and suppression of one thought with (another) thought, sweat flowed from my armpits.
mn85:20.5: Just as a strong man, Prince, after seizing a very weak man by the head, or seizing him by the body, would restrain, constrain and suppress him,
mn85:20.6: just so to me, Prince, with teeth clenched against teeth, with the tongue pressing on the palate, with complete restraint, constraint and suppression of one thought with (another) thought, sweat flowed from my armpits.
mn85:20.7: But although, Prince, my energy was strenuous and unshaken, and mindfulness was attended to and unconfused, my body was overstressed, not quietened, and therefore the effort I made was overwhelmed by the strain of exertion.
mn85:21.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:21.2: ‘What if I were to meditate on the breathless meditation?’
mn85:21.3: Then, Prince, I blocked the in-breath and out-breath at the mouth and at the nose.
mn85:21.4: Then to me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose, there was an excessive noise of wind escaping through the ears.
mn85:21.5: Just as there is an excessive noise from blowing on a smith’s bellows,
mn85:21.6: just so to me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose, there was an excessive noise of wind escaping through the ears.
mn85:21.7: But although for me, Prince, energy was strenuous and unshaken, and mindfulness was attended to and unconfused, my body was overstressed, not quietened, and therefore the effort I made was overwhelmed by the strain of exertion.
mn85:22.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:22.2: ‘What if I were to meditate on the breathless meditation?’
mn85:22.3: Then, Prince, I blocked the in-breath and out-breath at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears.
mn85:22.4: Then to me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears, excessive winds raged inside my head.
mn85:22.5: Just as though a strong man, Prince, were to cleave inside my head with a sharp pointed sword,
mn85:22.6: just so to me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears, excessive winds raged inside my head.
mn85:22.7: But although for me, Prince, energy was strenuous and unshaken, and mindfulness was attended to and unconfused, my body was overstressed, not quietened, and therefore the effort I made was overwhelmed by the strain of exertion.

mn85:23.3: Then, Prince, I blocked the in-breath and out-breath at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears.
mn85:23.4: Then to me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears, there was an excessive headache in my head.

mn85:24.3: Then, Prince, I blocked the in-breath and out-breath at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears.

mn85:25.2: ‘What if I were to meditate on the breathless meditation?’
mn85:25.3: Then, Prince, I blocked the in-breath and out-breath at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears.
mn85:25.4: Then to me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears, there was an excessive fever inside the body.
mn85:25.5: Just as though two strong men, Prince, after seizing a very weak man with their arms, were to burn and scorch him with embers,
mn85:25.6: so for me, Prince, with the in-breath and out-breath blocked at the mouth and at the nose and at the ears, there was an excessive fever inside the body.

mn85:26.1: Further, Prince, this occurred to the gods after seeing me:
mn85:26.4: ‘The ascetic Gotama has not died, he is dying,’
mn85:26.6: ‘The ascetic Gotama has not died, he is not dying, the ascetic Gotama is Worthy, it is in this way that the Worthy One lives.’
mn85:27.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:27.2: ‘What if I were to practice with cutting off food entirely?’
mn85:27.3: Then, Prince, some gods having approached, said this to me:
mn85:27.4: “Do not, Sir, practice with cutting off food entirely.
mn85:27.5: If, Sir, you will practice with cutting off food entirely, we will make you imbibe divine nutrient through the pores of your skin, and you will keep going.”
mn85:27.6: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:27.7: ‘If I were to claim I am entirely without food, and these gods were to make me imbibe divine nutrient through the pores of my skin, and I were to keep going, that would be a falsehood for me.”
mn85:27.8: Then, Prince, I rejected those gods, saying: “Why should I (do that)?”
mn85:28.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:28.2: ‘What if I were to take food little by little, measure by measure, whether it be mung bean soup, or vetch soup, or chick-pea soup, or pea soup?’
mn85:28.3: Then, Prince, I took food little by little, measure by measure, whether mung bean soup, or vetch soup, or chick-pea soup, or pea soup.
mn85:28.4: Then, Prince, as I took food little by little, measure by measure, whether mung bean soup, or vetch soup, or chick-pea soup, or pea soup, this body became excessively emaciated.
mn85:28.5: Just like vine knots or bamboo knots, so were my limbs both great and small through having so little food.
mn85:28.6: Just like a camel’s foot, so did my buttocks become through having so little food.
mn85:28.7: Just like a twisted vine, so did my backbone become twisted through having so little food.
mn85:28.8: Just like an old hall, in which the main beam is rotten and broken, so did my ribs become rotten and broken through having so little food.
mn85:28.9: Just like in a deep pool, the stars in the water are seen lying deep and distant, so in the sockets of my eyes, the pupils of my eyes were seen lying deep and distant through having so little food.
mn85:28.10: Just like a freshly cut bitter gourd will become withered and shrunken through wind and heat, so did the skin on my head become withered and shrunken through having so little food.
mn85:28.11: Then, Prince, thinking: ‘I will touch the skin of my stomach,’ I took ahold of my backbone, thinking: ‘I will touch my backbone,’ I took ahold of the skin of my stomach, so far, Prince, did the skin of my stomach and my backbone stick together through having so little food.
mn85:28.12: Then, Prince, thinking: ‘I will pass excrement or urine,’ I fell down face forward right there through having so little food.
mn85:28.13: Then, Prince, I rubbed this body and my limbs comfortably with my hand. Then, Prince, as I rubbed my limbs with my hand, hair that was rotten at the root fell out of my body through having so little food.
mn85:29.1: Further, Prince, this occurred to men after seeing me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is black,’
mn85:29.2: and to some men this occurred: ‘The ascetic Gotama is not black, the ascetic Gotama is brown,’
mn85:29.3: and to some men this occurred: ‘The ascetic Gotama is not black, he is not brown, the ascetic Gotama has golden skin.’
mn85:29.4: So far, Prince, was the pure and bright colour of my skin spoilt through having so little food.
mn85:30.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:30.2: ‘Those ascetics and priests in the past times who felt acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, there is nothing beyond or superior to this.
mn85:30.3: Those ascetics and priests in the future times who will feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, there is nothing beyond or superior to this.
mn85:30.4: Those ascetics and priests who now feel acute pain, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings, there is nothing beyond or superior to this.
mn85:30.5: But even by undergoing this bitter austerity I did not attain a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight.
mn85:30.6: I wonder is there another path to Awakening?’
mn85:31.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:31.2: ‘But I recall that while my Sakyan Father was at work, while I was sitting in the cool of the shade of the Rose-Apple tree, quite secluded from sense desires, secluded from unwholesome things, having thinking, reflection, and the happiness and rapture born of seclusion, I dwelt having attained the first absorption.
mn85:31.3: I wonder if this is the path to Awakening?’
mn85:31.4: Then to me, Prince, in conformity with that recollection I became conscious:
mn85:32.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:32.2: ‘Why am I afraid of that pleasure? That pleasure is one thing, and unwholesome sensual pleasures are another thing.’
mn85:32.3: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:32.4: ‘I am not afraid of that pleasure. That pleasure is one thing, and unwholesome sensual pleasures are another thing.’
mn85:33.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:33.2: ‘It is not easy to attain that pleasure with the body so excessively emaciated, what if I were to take gross food, boiled rice and milk?’
mn85:33.3: Then, Prince, I took gross food, boiled rice and milk.
mn85:33.4: But at that time, Prince, the group-of-five monks were present,
mn85:33.5: thinking: ‘This ascetic Gotama will attain Dhamma, and he will inform us.
mn85:33.6: When, Prince, I took gross food, boiled rice and milk, then the group-of-five monks being disgusted, left me,
mn85:33.7: thinking: ‘This ascetic Gotama is given to luxury, he has forsaken the striving, he has gone back to luxury.’
mn85:34-37.1: Then, Prince, having taken gross food and regained strength, quite secluded from sense desires, secluded from unwholesome things, having thinking, reflection, and the happiness and rapture born of seclusion, I dwelt having attained the first absorption.
mn85:34-37.2: With the ending of thinking, and reflection, with internal clarity, and one-pointedness of mind, being without thinking, without reflection, having the happiness and rapture born of concentration,
mn85:34-37.3: I dwelt having attained the second absorption. With the fading away of rapture I dwelt equanimous, mindful, clearly knowing, experiencing happiness through the body, about which the Noble Ones declare: “He lives pleasantly, mindful, and equanimous,” (thus) I dwelt having attained the third absorption. Having given up pleasure, given up pain, and with the previous disappearence of mental well-being and sorrow, without pain, without pleasure, and with complete purity of mindfulness owing to equanimity,
mn85:34-37.4: I dwelt having attained the fourth absorption.
mn85:34-37.5: Then with a mind well-concentrated, and complete purity that comes from a cleansed mind, being passionless, free of defilements, malleable, workable, steady, imperturbable, I directed my mind to knowledge and recall of previous existences.
mn85:34-37.6: I recollected various previous existences, such as: one life, two lives, three lives, four lives, five lives, ten lives, twenty lives, thirty lives, forty lives, fifty lives, a hundred lives, a thousand lives, a hundred thousand lives, innumerable aeons of devolution, innumerable aeons of evolution, innumerable aeons of devolution and evolution: in such and such a place I had this name, this family, this class, this food, this experience of pleasure and pain, this life term; passing away from there I arose in another state of existence, and in that place I had this name, this family, this class, this food, this experience of pleasure and pain, this life term, and passing away from there I arose here, and so with their characteristics and with their details I recollected my various previous existences.
mn85:34-37.7: This to me, Prince, in the first watch of the night, was the first knowledge I attained,
mn85:34-37.8: ignorance was abandoned, knowledge arose, darkness was abandoned, light arose, as I was living heedful, ardent, and resolute in this way.
mn85:38.1: Then with a mind well-concentrated, and complete purity that comes from a cleansed mind, being passionless, free of defilements, malleable, workable, steady, imperturbable, I directed my mind to knowledge of the passing away and rearising of beings.
mn85:38.2: With the divine eye which is purified and surpasses that of (normal) men I saw the passing away and arising of beings, inferior, superior, beautiful, ugly, in a good destiny, in a bad destiny, and I knew beings arise according to their (good and bad) actions: Those venerables who are endowed with bad bodily conduct, endowed with bad verbal conduct, endowed with bad mental conduct, who blamed the noble ones, were ones of wrong view, and undertook deeds based on wrong view, at the break-up of the body, after death, arise in the lower world, in an unhappy destiny, in the fall, in the nether regions, and those venerables who are endowed with good bodily conduct, endowed with good verbal conduct, endowed with good mental conduct, who did not blame the noble ones, were ones of right view, and undertook deeds based on right view, at the break-up of the body, after death, arise in a good destiny, a heavenly world.
mn85:39.1: This to me, Prince, in the middle watch of the night, was the second knowledge I attained, ignorance was abandoned, knowledge arose, darkness was abandoned, light arose, as I was living heedful, ardent, and resolute in this way.
mn85:40.1: Then with a mind well-concentrated, and complete purity that comes from a cleansed mind, being passionless, free of defilements, malleable, workable, steady, imperturbable, I directed my mind to knowledge about the destruction of the pollutants.
mn85:40.2: I knew, as it really is: ‘This is suffering,’ I knew, as it really is: ‘This is the arising of suffering,’ I knew, as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering,’ I knew, as it really is: ‘This is the practice going to the cessation of suffering,’
mn85:40.3: I knew, as it really is: ‘These are pollutants,’ I knew, as it really is: ‘This is the arising of pollutants,’ I knew, as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of pollutants,’ I knew, as it really is: ‘This is the practice going to the cessation of pollutants,’
mn85:41.1: Then knowing in this way, seeing in this way, my mind was free from the pollutant of sensuality, my mind was free from the pollutant of (craving for) continued existence, my mind was free from the pollutant of ignorance.
mn85:41.2: In freedom there was the knowledge: ‘(This is) freedom,’
mn85:41.3: ‘Destroyed is (re)birth, accomplished is the spiritual life, done is what ought to be done, there is no more of this mundane state,’ this I knew.
mn85:42.1: This to me, Prince, in the last watch of the night, was the third knowledge I attained,
mn85:42.2: ignorance was abandoned, knowledge arose, darkness was abandoned, light arose, as I was living heedful, ardent, and resolute in this way.
mn85:43.1: Then, Prince, this occurred to me:
mn85:43.2: ‘This Dhamma I have attained is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, excellent, beyond the sphere of logic, profound, understandable (only) by the wise.
mn85:43.3: But this generation delights in desire, is devoted to desire, gladdened by desire, and for this generation delighting in desire, devoted to desire, gladdened by desire,
mn85:43.4: this thing is hard to see, that is to say: conditionality and conditional origination.
mn85:43.5: This thing also is hard to see, that is to say: the tranquilising of all processes, the letting go of all bases for cleaving, the end of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.
mn85:43.6: But if I were to teach the Dhamma and others did not understand me that would be tiring for me, that would be troublesome to me.’
mn85:43.7: Further, Prince, these truly wonderful verses occurred to me, that were unheard of in the past:
mn85:43.8: ‘Now is it suitable for me to explain what was attained with difficulty?
mn85:43.10: For those overcome by passion and hatred
mn85:43.11: this Dhamma is not easily understood.
mn85:43.12: Going against the stream, it is profound, deep, hard to see, subtle.

mn85:43.16: Such was my reflection, Prince, and my mind inclined to inaction, not to teaching the Dhamma.
mn85:44.1: Then, Prince, to Brahmā Sahampati, knowing with his mind the reflection in my mind, this (thought) occurred:
mn85:44.2: ‘The world is surely going to destruction, the world is surely going to complete destruction, wherever the Realised One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha’s mind inclines to inaction, not to teaching the Dhamma.’
mn85:44.3: Then, Prince, Brahmā Sahampati, just as a strong man might stretch out a bent arm, or bend in an outstretched arm, so did he vanish from the Brahmā world and appear in front of me.
mn85:44.4: Then, Prince, Brahmā Sahampati, after arranging his upper robe on one shoulder, and raising his hands in respectful salutation, said this to me:
mn85:44.5: “Let the Fortunate One preach the Dhamma, reverend Sir, let the Happy One preach the Dhamma,
mn85:44.6: there are beings with little dust on the eyes who are perishing through not hearing the Dhamma,
mn85:44.7: there will be those who understand the Dhamma.”
mn85:44.9: and after saying this he said something more:
mn85:44.11: an impure Dhamma, invented by those still stained,
mn85:44.12: open the door to the Deathless,
mn85:44.13: let them hear the Dhamma understood by the Pure One.
mn85:44.14: As one who is standing on a rock on the top of a mountain
mn85:44.15: can see the people on all sides,
mn85:44.16: in the same way, One of Great Wisdom, having ascended
mn85:44.17: the Palace made from Dhamma, Visionary One,
mn85:44.18: look down on the people overcome by grief,
mn85:44.19: One Free of Grief, on those overcome by birth and old-age.
mn85:44.20: Rise up, O Hero, Victorious in Battle.
mn85:44.21: Caravan-Leader, Debtless One, travel through the world.
mn85:44.22: Let the Fortunate One teach the Dhamma,
mn85:44.23: there will be those who understand.”
mn85:45.1: Then, Prince, having understood Brahmā’s request, out of kindness I looked at beings around the world with my Buddha-eye.
mn85:45.2: While looking around the world, Prince, with my Buddha-eye, I saw beings having little dust on the eyes, having great dust on the eyes, having sharp faculties, having undeveloped faculties, having good conditions, having poor conditions, easy to instruct, hard to instruct, and (only) some who dwelt seeing danger in what is blameworthy and in the next world.
mn85:45.3: Just as with water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses some of those water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses, born in the water, flourishing in the water, not rising above water, are nourished from inside the depths, some of those water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses, born in the water, flourishing in the water, surrounded by water, stand level with the water, some of those water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses, born in the water, flourishing in the water, stand above the water, and are untouched by the water.
mn85:45.4: Even so while looking around the world, Prince, with my Buddha-eye, I saw beings having little dust on the eyes, having great dust on the eyes, having sharp faculties, having undeveloped faculties, having good conditions, having poor conditions, easy to instruct, hard to instruct, and (only) some who dwelt seeing danger in what is blameworthy and in the next world.
mn85:45.5: Then, Prince, I recited this verse to Brahmā Sahampati:
mn85:45.6: “Open for you are the doors to the Deathless,
mn85:45.7: whoever has ears let them release their faith.
mn85:45.8: Perceiving trouble, Brahmā, I did not speak amongst humans,
mn85:45.9: about what was hard-learned, the excellent Dhamma!”
mn85:45.10: Then, Prince, Brahmā Sahampati, thinking: ‘I have obtained consent for the Fortunate One to teach the Dhamma,’ after worshipping and circumambulating me, vanished right there.

mn85:50.1: Then, Prince, while I was walking gradually on walking tour, I approached Bārāṇasī, Isipatana, the Deer Park, and the group-of-five monks.
mn85:50.2: The group-of-five monks, Prince, saw me coming from afar,
mn85:50.3: and after seeing (me), they resolved among themselves:
mn85:50.4: “This Ascetic Gotama who is coming, friends, is given to luxury, forsaking the striving he has gone back to luxury.
mn85:50.5: He should certainly not be worshipped or stood up for, nor should his bowl and robe be taken,
mn85:50.6: however, we can prepare a seat, if he wishes he will sit down.”
mn85:50.7: As I approached, Prince, the group-of-five monks were unable to continue with their own agreement,

mn85:51.1: When this was said, Prince, I said this to the group-of-five monks:
mn85:51.2: “Do not address the Fortunate One, monks, by name and by the word ‘friend’,
mn85:51.3: the Realised One, monks, is a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha.
mn85:51.4: Lend an ear, monks, I will instruct you about the attainment of the Deathless, I will teach the Dhamma,
mn85:51.5: (and) following the path as it has been preached, after no long time in regard to that good for which young men of good family rightly go forth from the home to the homeless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life, you will dwell having known, experienced, and attained it yourselves in this very life.”
mn85:51.6: When this was said, Prince, the group-of-five monks said this to me:
mn85:51.7: “But you, friend Gotama, by that (ascetic) lifestyle, that practice, that difficult way of living, did not attain states beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight. mn85:58.1: “Thus, Prince, there are these five qualities of striving.
mn85:58.3: Here, Prince, a monk has faith, he believes in the Realised One’s Awakening thus:
mn85:58.4: Such is he, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha, the one endowed with understanding and good conduct, the Happy One, the one who understands the worlds, the Teacher of gods and men, the Buddha, the Fortunate One, the unsurpassed guide for those people who need taming.
mn85:58.5: He is one with few afflictions and little illness, endowed with good digestion and metabolism, neither too cool nor too hot, but in the middle, and suitable for striving.
mn85:58.6: He is not treacherous or deceitful and shows himself as he really is to his teachers and his wise spiritual friends.
mn85:58.7: He lives energetically, giving up unwholesome things, and undertaking wholesome things, steadfast, making strong effort, not abandoning responsibility regarding wholesome things.
mn85:58.8: He is wise, endowed with wisdom regarding rising and falling, regarding noble penetration, regarding what leads to the complete destruction of suffering.
mn85:58.9: These, Prince, are the five qualities of striving.

mn85:60.1: When this was said, Prince Bodhi said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:60.2: “Oh, the Buddha, oh the Dhamma, oh the well-taught Dhamma!
mn85:60.3: Indeed, instructed in the evening he can attain distinction by morning, instructed in the morning he can attain distinction by evening!”
mn85:61.1: When this was said, the student Sañjikāputta said this to Prince Bodhi:

mn85:61.5: “Do not say that, dear Sañjikāputta, do not say that, dear Sañjikāputta.
mn85:61.6: Face-to-face, dear Sañjikāputta, I heard this from my Noble Mother, face-to-face I learned it:
mn85:61.7: At one time, dear Sañjikāputta, the Fortunate One was dwelling near Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery.
mn85:61.8: Then my Noble Mother, who was pregnant, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, she sat down on one side. While sitting on one side my Noble Mother said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:61.9: ‘Whatever this is, reverend Sir, in my womb, a boy or a girl, he goes to the reverend Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
mn85:61.10: Please bear in mind that he is a lay disciple who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as he has the breath of life.’
mn85:61.11: At one time, dear Sañjikāputta, ‘the Fortunate One was dwelling here amongst the Bhaggas in the Deer Park in Bhesakaḷā’s Wood on the Crocodile Hill.
mn85:61.12: Then my nurse, carrying me on her hip, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, she stood on one side. While standing on one side my nurse said this to the Fortunate One:
mn85:61.13: ‘This Prince Bodhi, reverend Sir, goes to the reverend Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
mn85:61.14: Please bear in mind that he is a lay disciple who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as he has the breath of life.’
mn85:61.15: Now today, dear Sañjikāputta, for a third time I go to the reverend Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
mn85:61.16: Please bear in mind that I am a lay disciple who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I have the breath of life.”
mn85:61.17: The Discourse to Prince Bodhi is Finished
